sentences.text: Caseosaurus was a small, lightly built, bipedal carnivore that lived on the ground and could reach a length of 2 meters.
Size estimates indicate this animal grew up to 2 meters long and weighed no more than 50 kilograms.
The genus was formally described and named by Hunt, Lucas, Heckert, Sullivan, and Lockley in 1998, honoring the scientist Ermine Cowles Case.
The specific name crosbyensis refers to Crosby County in Texas, where the fossils were discovered.
The genus is known from a single specimen, an isolated hip bone measuring nearly 141 millimeters.
In 2018, Caseosaurus was re-evaluated as a valid species identified as a relative of Herrerasaurus, placing it outside the Dinosauria.
It is classified within the family Herrerasauridae.
In 2004, Langer examined the holotype ilium and reassigned it to the genus Chindesaurus, leading to suggestions that Caseosaurus might be the same dinosaur as Chindesaurus.
Caseosaurus lived during the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 235 to 228 million years ago, in what is now North America.
The paleoenvironment included the archosaur Tecovasaurus and other early theropods that left preserved bipedal tracks.

Irmis et al. concluded that an ilium originally assigned to Eucoelophysis strongly resembles the Caseosaurus holotype, while a recent review classified Caseosaurus as a nomen dubium, contradicting earlier studies that validated it.
